<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">The most common reply I get when I run this offer is some version of: “I’ve been meaning to upgrade but kept putting it off.”</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">I get it. It never feels urgent until something breaks.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Here’s what I’ve noticed. The people who upgrade to annual aren’t the ones who <em>need it most urgently.</em> They’re the ones who’ve already been using the free version for a while, already know what the platform does, and just decide to stop putting it off.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">You know what Ubersuggest does. You’ve run the reports. You’ve seen the data.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">For <strong>$16/month</strong>, the annual plan gives you everything and saves you 5 months versus paying monthly. </p>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;margin:0 auto"><tbody><tr><td>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Your paid search campaigns didn’t suddenly get worse. The environment around them changed.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">CPCs are rising.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">CTR is dropping.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Performance feels harder to scale.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But here’s what’s actually happening:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Users aren’t searching the same way anymore. They’re asking.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">AI tools like ChatGPT and Google’s AI Overviews are answering questions *before* someone ever clicks an ad.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">This is the shift most marketers are missing:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">You’re no longer competing for a position. You’re competing to be included in the answer.</p>

<p style="line-height:150%; font-weight:bold">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="line-height:150%">Discover how professional buyers evaluate high-growth Amazon businesses by looking beyond basic revenue to assess long-term stability and risk.</p>
<p style="line-height:150%">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="line-height:150%">In our latest webinar you'll discover the four critical "hidden" areas:</p>
<ul style="line-height:150%">
<li>
<p style="line-height:150%">Financial health, where metrics like marketing efficiency (PPC-to-revenue ratios) and true EBITDA are scrutinized</p>
</li>
<li>
<p style="line-height:150%">Risk mitigation, which focuses on reducing SKU concentration and clearing aged inventory</p>
</li>
<li>
<p style="line-height:150%">Meticulous documentation, requiring a clear paper trail for every expense to prove the business's valuation</p>
</li>
<li>
<p style="line-height:150%">Scalability, where buyers look for a credible path to growth through marketplace diversification (like TikTok or Shopify) and reduced founder reliance.</p>
</li>
</ul>

<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Everyone’s talking about Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">And yes, AI is changing how people discover things.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But here’s the reality:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Google still handles 13.7+ billion searches a day. AI is growing fast, but search is still where demand starts.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">What is changing is this:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">AI Overviews are taking over the results page. And when they show up, users don’t click around. They read the summary and trust the sources it cites.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Those citations?</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">That’s the new “blue link.” If you’re not included, you’re invisible.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">We’re already helping clients adapt.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Take <a href="https://e22d5796.click.convertkit-mail4." target="_blank" class="ck-link" rel="noopener noreferrer" url-id="1847791513">Vinyl Institute</a>.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">We didn’t rely on ads or hacks. We focused on:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Authoritative, intent-driven content</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Strong E-E-A-T signals (expertise, trust, credibility)</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Structuring content for both search engines and AI systems</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">The result:</p>
<ul class="unordered_list">
<li class="list_item"><span>A 4,540% increase in Google AI Overview Citations</span></li>
<li class="list_item"><span>Stronger presence in high-intent searches</span></li>
<li class="list_item"><span>Clear authority in their category</span></li>
</ul>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">It’s about being cited, trusted, and chosen. Across Google and AI.</p>

<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Most marketing reports look good.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Traffic is up. Conversions look steady. ROAS seems strong.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But here’s the truth:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">They’re often misleading. Because you aren’t seeing your revenue go up.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">My team breaks all of this down in a <a href="https://e22d5796.click.convertkit-mail4." target="_blank" class="ck-link" rel="noopener noreferrer" url-id="1847501665">recent post</a>.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Here’s what’s going wrong:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">❌ Attribution is flawed</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">❌Tracking is incomplete</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">❌And many metrics are easy to game</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">So you end up scaling what looks good…</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Not what actually drives revenue.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">The shift smart companies are making:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔️Measuring incrementality (what actually drives growth)</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔️Focusing on revenue and profit—not just conversions</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔️Prioritizing customer quality and lifetime value</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Because marketing isn’t about dashboards. <em>It’s about results.</em></p>

   <tr style=border:0>
      <td class=bodySection style="border:0; color:#444444; padding:0 50px 30px 50px">
         <table cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0 border=0 width=100% style="border:0; border-collapse:collapse; border-spacing:0; color:#202124; font-family:Google Sans, Arial, sans-serif; font-size:18px; line-height:27px;">

           <!-- FIRST PARAGRAPH -->
           <tr style=border:0>
               <td align=left style="border:0; padding-top: 8px; padding-bottom: 8px;"><section>
                  <p class=para style="color:#202124; font-family:Google Sans, Arial, sans-serif; font-size:18px; line-height:27px; margin:16px 0 16px 0; padding:0">Hello,<br>
<br>
For customers who have linked Google Analytics and Google Ads accounts, we are simplifying controls and streamlining the consent process. For linked properties, Google Ads settings will exclusively control the usage of data in Google Ads in accordance with users’ consent choices. Customers remain in control of if and how their data is collected, and can change their settings at any time. For more information, please see the <a href=https://c.gle/ADMV5J9nVbJ4drblAharG-VpFx5UV6l0aj4DzVTOXgldBz-0y4I_B6x17mVixCjFsa3Z0ECF0DiJM4x4gpJ7RhSaVvay0xLWlAWa5jA1al6VvU95P9Wg4hT2J06-rW7qxUUL_24jn3xu1DQa_CCa50FM0JHP0BvZwS9dLLgbu90KdEuxL1EieIMHTDaKBHXifzP5R8uAnzpFvj-gGyPVkUopgNDfsrg style="color:#448aff; text-decoration:none;" target=_blank><span>help center announcement</span></a>.</p></section>
               </td>
           </tr>
           <!-- SECOND PARAGRAPH -->
           <tr style=border:0>
               <td align=left style="border:0; padding-top: 8px; padding-bottom: 8px;"><section>
                  <p class=para style="color:#202124; font-family:Google Sans, Arial, sans-serif; font-size:18px; line-height:27px; margin:0 0 16px 0; padding:0"><b>What is changing?</b><br>
The first change to support this direction is an update to the Google Signals setting in Google Analytics. Today, the collection of Google Ads cookies and IDs from the Google Analytics tag and <a href=https://c.gle/ADMV5J8O8GQtoxKuYjPCQ1qYLV8s3pAJGYOADvtR9jKzk38uvIZ9OkA3-00ybfpKgm4dmk_T_Z-p4PP0yJNwxAEBJjWMuo88ghja-BcFjXgWQp03OYoeSiIRua5sLcpjrWC8kJFdNcO1PdO8f13zAk11P5pB9iDGm5PqPS1Y style="color:#448aff; text-decoration:none;" target=_blank><span>Firebase SDK</span></a> is controlled by both the Google Signals setting in Google Analytics and your <a href=https://c.gle/ADMV5J9yqz4QDThxbkyceNgHu77catvZbz27rVFLh3TcPKDO-fUEObM0ghjTfbGdiRlj4ZPZbb71Ooe_nmQsnd0Cdj3BbHKotd_INC9w2Qc1GIKrCC9yARhDATZOshT29JF5pXw9Sg56_SBJXmAX9-yHoNGUkYz8R7_WYBSTv1AKrYPtjO5VKkfrDY61QfqE0vWESQ style="color:#448aff; text-decoration:none;" target=_blank><span>Consent Mode</span></a> Ads settings. This applies to its usage for both Google Analytics and Google Ads.<br>
<br>
Starting 15 June ‘26, our tags and SDKs will apply destination-specific controls. This means that when the data is used in Google Analytics, the Google Signals setting and <a href=https://c.gle/ADMV5J87UxBXeP_fwQeW72apnTSf1zp_cy-epgSv3vuhyHdsE1CKzX5ZlKHgkRvtSGBH5BzTaspNIY1d3nGiwwulRIKsxSEiKacjvVwIzugAx1B5bJPSMMRZZyC-Ry5uXcQEL58WK5TM-fUWaY4nul3xfcU-FqudL0LTk8B7CUmY-wANRzN3Zd221f_B1ZFkrW9zQb9xVcv3bqM2c3w5mjbdGa8sQQEG9UUaFimu1wPTRRQI8M7GJjo07Rk style="color:#448aff; text-decoration:none;" target=_blank><span>API</span></a> will control usage. When data is used in Google Ads (including data shared from Google Analytics), it will be exclusively controlled by the Ads Consent Mode. This ensures that a user’s advertising preferences continue to be the primary control for ad-related data usage.<br>
<br>
<b>Why we are doing this</b>: Our goal is to provide a simpler and more streamlined experience for both you and your users. By aligning our systems to look at a single consent setting, we remove inconsistencies between your Google Analytics and Ads accounts while making it easier for you to honor user privacy preferences with confidence and clarity.</p></section>
               </td>

           <tr style=border:0>
               <td align=left style="border:0; padding-top: 8px; padding-bottom: 8px;"><section>
                  <p class=para style="color:#202124; font-family:Google Sans, Arial, sans-serif; font-size:18px; line-height:27px; margin:0 0 16px 0; padding:0"><b>What actions do I need to take?</b><br>
If you currently have Google Signals <span style="font-weight: bold; color:#38761d;">turned on</span>, no action is needed. There will be no changes to your data behavior.<br>
<br>
If you currently have Google Signals <span style="font-weight: bold; color:#990000;">turned off</span>, Ads will begin using Ads cookies if your users consent to ad_storage. Web and app activity with ad_storage granted will be associated with Google’s signed in user information to improve your audiences, bidding, optimization, and conversion measurement. The Google Signals setting will no longer control these capabilities.<br>
<br>
If you do not want Google Ads to use these cookies and IDs, you can set the default state for Consent Mode ad_storage to “denied.” These defaults can be set regionally:
<ol>
	<li><a href=https://c.gle/ADMV5J8vfm4YsBJBjSh7ci9SUkzKJC-xVobRykkTxwJ3rX4TsA1GjHGso5hIKmnEVZTdIF06tn2r8zT3UXkoBjUYbAOhf_isNkaSb1ryrNnjDuBEhuqfYBvUrtnom0U8a2CFcvvg9QqDcgIA_rBe8suI1LElmG42E-jRKGCS0_mxdRqgUcyrvu6nN_cIrehLeB5fQxUBBZBzoG79DRKUDRw_1ThkT9dHF5LkMxXsAisyH3F6VYdSJn94qb3DYZlwYL3QcE7z style="color:#448aff; text-decoration:none;" target=_blank><span>Set the default consent state for websites</span></a></li>
	<li><a href=https://c.gle/ADMV5J8bseAgdfAXSjcfyfdJoleVUwkh5KzPCctJYXC-PEMBN5npnVPpGKTgVUjZte5szAbB8qefl-1WtA50xTBI5Nr2RA5AGcnEdieQEY3A8vSE4JYPfhVPN-7fhoTpM09zhRtUPWb73Vy9-x7tGWiP6hrxNUXn0Z76OwCT2jYFLRReXQpJPE4JKXk_tlVBahyM7HT0bMBCNK9-2b7WEnOPMLBdK2ULqXRJEO9FldooKzwoVMSb1qFhVG7T1Jm_FIh7H6X0D0g-t5IwVBXVWRhiCiI style="color:#448aff; text-decoration:none;" target=_blank><span>Set the default consent state for apps</span></a></li></ol></p></section>
               </td>
           </tr>

               <td align=left style="border:0; padding-top: 8px; padding-bottom: 8px;"><section>
                  <p class=para style="color:#202124; font-family:Google Sans, Arial, sans-serif; font-size:18px; line-height:27px; margin:0 0 16px 0; padding:0"><span style="font-style: italic;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; color:#cc0000;">Important</span>: Changing Consent Mode ad_storage to denied prevents the collection and usage of all advertising cookies and device identifiers from your website or app. This action applies to all data collected by Ads and will significantly impact advertising measurement and conversion tracking, and hinder the performance of your campaigns within your linked Ads account.</span><br>

<b>Our commitment to transparency and control:</b> We are making these updates to empower you and your users with simpler data choices. Users will continue to have full control over if and how their data is collected. SAVE</span></a></p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">To investors,</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The United States and Iran were set to solidify the ceasefire with a peace agreement negotiated in Pakistan over the last few days. Vice President JD Vance stepped up to the podium after 21 hours of negotiations and informed the world there would be no peace deal.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Iran reportedly continues to refuse the US proposal, so the war is back on again. This time there is a big wrinkle though.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Rather than allow Iran to close the Strait of Hormuz, the United States has decided to implement a blockade of their own. At first glance, this seems like a childish decision to merely claim victory in a skirmish, but upon further review there is strategic importance to the decision.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>For example, Iran has not completely closed the Strait over the last few weeks. Instead, they have prevented most ships from passing through the waterway and they have merely been taxing other ships. This selective enforcement has been a big financial boost for the Middle Eastern country, especially because Iran has also been exporting their own oil through the Strait at the same time.</span><br><br><span>Rather than allow Iran to call the shots in the Strait, and continue to profit from their decisions, the United States blockade will rapidly cut off all economic benefit to Iran. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/28ab5848-c9b1-4c82-9398-0f6370a5c198?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">FDD Senior Fellow Miad Maleki writes</a><span> </span><em>&#8220;The U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz would cost Iran approximately $276 million per day in lost exports and disrupt $159 million per day in imports, a combined economic damage of ~$435 million per day, or $13 billion per month.&#8221;</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">This level of economic loss should apply maximum pressure to the country, along with exasperate the pain for Iran&#8217;s allies such as China. The decision for Iran to weaponize the Strait of Hormuz never really made sense, because they couldn&#8217;t deliver on their threats in the way people thought. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/e5418413-fc00-4e8d-90ba-5eeb24843fbd?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">Hudson Institute&#8217;s Zineb Riboua writes</a><span>:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ff6b00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em><span>&#8220;Iran&#8217;s move to weaponize the Strait of Hormuz ranks among its most strategically reckless decisions.</span><br><br><span>They cannot sustain control over it. Their military position does not allow for prolonged enforcement against determined opposition. More importantly, it was never a credible bargaining chip. Once escalated, it has to be relinquished without meaningful concessions. The only asset that has ever carried real negotiating weight is the nuclear program.</span><br><br><span>The logic behind the move is also flawed. The expectation was to trigger a global economic shock large enough to force a halt in U.S. operations. That outcome has not materialized. Instead, it has accelerated the opposite dynamic. Regional and global actors are now investing in routes and infrastructure designed to bypass the Strait altogether.</span><br><br><span>In trying to turn Hormuz into leverage, Iran is diminishing its long-term strategic value. Very stupid of IRGC.&#8221;</span></em></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">You can read about the geopolitical implications to this decision elsewhere, so I want to focus our time on how this development will impact the US economy and American citizens at home.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">First, the United States has become the most popular girl at the bar when it comes to selling oil. There are hundreds of tankers from around the world that are rushing to the Gulf of America to purchase oil from us. Whether this was an intended outcome or not, America&#8217;s energy independence is quickly becoming a strategic asset that will drive significant revenue growth for our oil and gas industry, along with our country.</p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: 100%;margin: 0 auto;"><table class="image-wrapper" width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" data-component-name="Image2ToDOMStatic" style="mso-padding-alt: 1em 0 1.6em;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"></td><td class="content" align="left" width="1200" style="text-align: center;"><a class="image-link" target="_blank" href="https://substack.com/redirect/180d831e-5993-4d81-bdb1-ef3376f955c3?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="position: relative;flex-direction: short-term military and operational costs for mine clearance, escorting ships, and potential combat with Iranian forces. These additional costs will only put more pressure on the national debt, which will lead to further debasement of the US dollar over the long run. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Third, oil prices will likely continue to be very volatile. The entire world is trying to figure out what the price for a barrel of oil should be, but the input costs, the available global supply, and the future prospects of production continue to change on a daily basis. There is consensus belief that a fully opened Strait will lead to lower oil prices, so a fully closed Strait will only continue to put upwards pressure on prices. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Fourth, the US stock market will be volatile. There is lots of pressure on software stocks and the tech industry more broadly, while energy and oil company stocks have been outperforming in recent weeks. These trends could reverse if the war ends, but it seems like we are in a state of volatility for the foreseeable future. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Lastly, there will be a mixed message in the domestic economy. As I wrote about last week, </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/ee1cf5fe-4f48-440a-a119-c74c0085d62e?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">the US economy will continue profiting from higher oil prices</a><span>, while American citizens feel the pain at the pump. This will feed the higher inflation narrative, especially as people brace for higher fertilizer prices, higher food prices, and higher shipping costs globally. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">There is no way to spin the negative impact on US households in the short-term. The big question becomes how transient this impact will be? Once the war is over, do prices come back down quickly? Do Americans get amnesia and forget about this episode if the stock market rips higher over the summer? How do the midterm elections play into the geopolitical options that President Trump and his administration are weighing?</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I don&#8217;t have answers to many of these questions. But it is clear that the US blockade is going to change the calculus for Iran in this conflict. They just went from being in charge to being cut off from the world. Regardless of what they say publicly, no one loses $13 billion per month and shrugs it off. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Lets just hope that we see a true ceasefire as a result of this latest escalation. War is an ugly thing and no one wants to see innocent people dying. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Hope you all have a great start to your week. I will talk to everyone tomorrow. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em><strong>- Anthony J. <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;margin:0 auto"><tbody><tr><td>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Your paid search campaigns didn’t suddenly get worse. The system around them changed.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">CPCs are up. CTRs are down.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">And most teams are responding the same way:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Optimize more. Test more. push harder.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But the issue isn’t effort. It’s that users aren’t behaving the same way anymore.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">They’re not searching. They’re asking.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">AI is answering questions before people ever click.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Now, here’s the important part: Paid search still works.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">In fact, for newer brands without strong organic visibility, it’s often the fastest way to capture demand.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But it’s no longer the first touchpoint.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">In my next webinar I will break down what’s happening and how to adapt.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">​<a href="https://e22d5796.click.convertkit-mail4.com/92um34ndl6unh6rde3ru9hzqndx24bwhg2l8/wnh2hghq7znmp8a7/aHR0cHM6Ly9hZHZhbmNlZC5ucGRpZ2l0YWwuY29tL3BhaWQtc2VhcmNoLWlzbnQtd2hhdC1pdC11c2VkLXRvLWJlLWxpdmUtd2ViaW5hci8_" target="_blank" class="ck-link" rel="noopener noreferrer" url-id="1847198436"><strong>Paid Search Isn’t What It Used to Be: The LLM Shift Explained</strong></a>​</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Tuesday, April 21 at 8 a.m. PDT</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">You’ll learn:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Why paid search feels less predictable (even when it’s working)</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ How AI is intercepting users earlier in the journey</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Where paid search still delivers the most value</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ How to adapt your strategy without rebuilding everything</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">You’re not just competing for clicks anymore. You’re competing to be included in the decision.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">👉 <a href="https://e22d5796.click.convertkit-mail4.com/92um34ndl6unh6rde3ru9hzqndx24bwhg2l8/wnh2hghq7znmp8a7/aHR0cHM6Ly9hZHZhbmNlZC5ucGRpZ2l0YWwuY29tL3BhaWQtc2VhcmNoLWlzbnQtd2hhdC1pdC11c2VkLXRvLWJlLWxpdmUtd2ViaW5hci8_" target="_blank" class="ck-link" rel="noopener noreferrer" url-id="1847198436"><strong>Save your seat here</strong></a>.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">See you there,</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Neil Patel</p>

<p style="line-height:150%"><span style="font-weight: bold;">Unlock Your Exit: The Hidden Metrics That Drive 7-Figure Amazon Valuations</span></p>
<p style="line-height:150%"><br>What separates a stagnant Amazon brand from a high-premium exit? It isn’t just revenue—it’s risk-adjusted return. Buyers look beyond the dashboard, scrutinizing four critical areas: SKU concentration, owner dependency, aged inventory, and documentation clarity.</p>
<p style="line-height:150%">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="line-height:150%">To maximize your multiple, you must "launch employees, not products." Transitioning from a solo operator to a system-led brand reduces "founder risk," attracting cash offers over complex earnouts. By optimizing imagery, diversifying into TikTok Shop, and cleaning your EBITDA of personal expenses, you transform a job into a transferable asset ready for a top-dollar sale.</p>
<p style="line-height:150%">&nbsp;</p>

16px;line-height: 26px;"><div class="body markup" dir="auto" style="text-align: initial;font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;width: 100%;word-break: break-word;margin-bottom: 16px;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin-top: 0;">To investors,</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I normally don&#8217;t write a letter to you on Sunday morning, but I wanted to highlight a very interesting research report that came from </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/56c193d4-a160-41a7-9fc3-d73711d56b7e?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">ProCap Insights</a><span> over the past week. The report looks at the impact of AI on the job market, including an analysis of whether artificial intelligence is stealing human jobs. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>One of the most eye-opening conclusions was artificial intelligence has a disproportionate negative impact on young people compared to their older peers. </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/c2925839-8c42-4c34-8501-3937e5fd3ffb?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;">The report explains</a><span>:</span></p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ff6b00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>In August 2025, researchers at the Stanford Digital Economy Lab published what may be the most important labor market study of the AI era. Erik Brynjolfsson, Chinchih Chen, and others analyzed employment trends across occupations ranked by AI exposure. Their findings shatter both narratives simultaneously.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>Workers aged 22 to 25 in the most AI-exposed occupations experienced a 16% relative decline in employment since late 2022, after controlling for firm-level shocks. Young software developers specifically saw employment fall 20% below its late fall 2022 peak by mid-2025. Early-career customer service workers declined 11% from their November 2022 peak.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>But workers aged 30 and over in those exact same high-AI-exposure occupations saw employment grow between 6% and 12% over the same period. The labor market did not shrink in these sectors. It bifurcated.</em></p></blockquote><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: 100%;margin: 0 auto;"><table class="image-wrapper" width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" data-component-name="Image2ToDOMStatic" style="mso-padding-alt: 1em 0 1.6em;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"></td><td class="content" align="left" width="1390" style="text-align: center;"><a class="image-link" target="_blank" href="https://substack.com/redirect/139f78c5-78f9-4ca6-b462-a53cd70f01ac?j=eyJ1IjoiM2hhNmhxIn0.fGjLyd93AVW2aVkcEYUIldVPqY9OipuTNb2QRZyO0uU" rel="" style="position: relative;flex-direction: column;align-items: center;padding: 0;width: auto;height: auto;border: none;text-decoration: none;display: block;margin: 0;"><img class="wide-image" data-attrs="{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/d6ba17d3-4a10-41b0-a693-7237190e48c9_1390x1018.png&quot;,&quot;srcNoWatermark&quot;:null,&quot;fullscreen&quot;:null,&quot;imageSize&quot;:null,&quot;height&quot;:1018,&quot;width&quot;:1390,&quot;resizeWidth&quot;:null,&quot;bytes&quot;:164745,&quot;alt&quot;:null,&quot;title&quot;:null,&quot;type&quot;:&quot;image/png&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:null,&quot;belowTheFold&quot;:false,&quot;topImage&quot;:true,&quot;internalRedirect&quot;:&quot;https://pomp.substack.com/i/193966186?img=https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd6ba17d3-4a10-41b0-a693-7237190e48c9_1390x1018.png&quot;,&quot;isProcessing&quot;:false,&quot;align&quot;:null,&quot;offset&quot;:false}" alt="" width="550" height="402.80575539568343" src="https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!22kn!,w_1100,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd6ba17d3-4a10-41b0-a693-7237190e48c9_1390x1018.png" style="border: none !important;vertical-align: middle;display: block;-ms-interpolation-mode: bicubic;height: auto;margin-bottom: 0;width: auto !important;max-width: 100% !important;margin: 0 auto;"></a></td><td style="text-align: center;"></td></tr></tbody></table></figure></div><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ff6b00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>The mechanism is consistent with how AI tools interact with the labor force. AI handles a growing share of rules-based, structured tasks traditionally assigned to junior workers, from drafting emails and writing boilerplate code to summarizing documents and handling tier-one customer queries. Senior workers, whose value comes from tacit knowledge, judgment, and soft skills, are not displaced by these same tools.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>They are augmented by it. One experienced developer with Copilot produces what previously required a team of three juniors.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>JPMorgan&#8217;s Aliaga found the same dynamic. Over one-third of U.S. workers now use generative AI for job tasks, but the St. Louis Fed estimates generative AI accounts for just 5.7% of total work hours as of mid-2025. That 5.7% falls disproportionately on the repetitive, entry-level work that defined the first rung of most professional careers.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>Goldman Sachs estimates that two-thirds of U.S. occupations have AI exposure, but only 6% to 7% of workers face genuine displacement risk. The rest face augmentation, and augmentation benefits the experienced.</em></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">This data makes sense when you realize that artificial intelligence is going to eat into the work force from the bottom up. As the technology improves, it will take over more complex and senior tasks, but until we reach that level of innovation it will be the young people who are affected the most. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">But the story is not only age-specific. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The ProCap Insights report, which is generated through an agentic AI system, identifies major pain underway in the publishing and media industries. The report explains:</p><blockquote style="border-left: 4px solid #ff6b00;margin: 20px 0;padding: 0;"><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>BLS establishment survey data reveals which sectors are already living in the post-AI labor market. Motion picture and sound recording employment has fallen 18.9% since January 2023, from 415,900 to 337,400 workers. Publishing industries employment declined 5.8% over the same period, from 958,500 to 902,800. These are content-creation sectors where AI tools directly substitute for junior and mid-level creative labor.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>Meanwhile, professional, scientific, and technical services, the largest white-collar sector, grew just 0.9% over three years. That 0.9% translates to roughly 97,000 jobs added in a sector of 10.8 million, a pace that barely keeps up with population growth.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>The sector is not contracting. It is calcifying.</em></p></blockquote><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: 100%;margin: 0 auto;"><table 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>The Harvard Business School research published in March 2026 reinforces this. Analyzing nearly all U.S. job postings from 2019 through March 2025, researchers found that automation-prone roles saw a 13% decrease in postings since ChatGPT&#8217;s launch, while analytical, technical, and creative roles saw a 20% increase. Job postings for automation-prone occupations also required 7% fewer skills.</em></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);margin-left: 20px;line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><em>Employers are not just posting fewer jobs. They are posting simpler ones, consistent with AI tools absorbing the complexity that once required a dedicated human.</em></p></blockquote><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Generative AI is very good at producing content, so it makes sense that content-focused industries are coming under pressure. Remember, this is the worse the technology will ever be, so we should expect an acceleration from here. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I continue to tell people that three areas of media will be safe from AI disruption: scoops, long-form profiles, and live coverage. But I believe people can insulate themselves from being negatively affected by AI if they can become AI proficient. There is not a company in the world that is going to fire employees who are the best at using AI internally. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Instead, companies are going to promote these people, give them more responsibilities, and likely pay them more money over time. Don&#8217;t sit around and be disrupted. Learn to use the tools and technology. This is true whether you are a professional investor or a casual individual investor. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Superhuman intelligence is now abundantly available. The only limiting factor is your curiosity and persistence.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Before I let you go, I highly suggest subscribing to ProCap Insights. <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;margin:0 auto"><tbody><tr><td>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Your best blog posts are probably losing traffic right now.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">It happens to everyone. Google favors fresh content. So the posts that were crushing it six months ago? They’re slowly sliding down the rankings while newer content takes their place.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Most people respond by writing more new content. That’s the hard way. The easy way? Update what you already have.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">A refreshed post with new stats, new examples, and a few additional keyword variations can jump right back to where it was, and sometimes higher. Google sees the updated timestamp, re-crawls the page, and re-evaluates it against the competition.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">I do this with my own content every single month. It’s the highest-ROI activity in my entire SEO strategy.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Try this right now:</p>
<ul class="unordered_list">
<li class="list_item"><span>Go to your Ubersuggest dashboard and click <a href="https://e22d5796.click.convertkit-mail4.com/92um34ndl6unh6rpx2ga9hzq3m9w5twhg2l8/n2hohvhvqlp505b6/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAubmVpbHBhdGVsLmNvbS9lbi9wb3NpdGlvbl90cmFja2luZy9yZWNlbnQ_dXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXVzLW1rdC1jYW1wYWlnbnMtbXFsLXllYXJseS10b29scy1lbWFpbC1uZWlsLWNrJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PWNvbnRlbnQtcmVmcmVzaCZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9Y29udmVydGtpdC1saXN0JnV0bV90ZXJtPWNrLWFwci0xMC0yNg==" target="_blank" class="ck-link" rel="noopener noreferrer" url-id="1846571140">Rank Tracking</a>.</span></li>
<li class="list_item"><span>Sort by <em>position dropped.</em></span></li>
<li class="list_item"><span>Pick the top 3 pages that slipped and update them this week.</span></li>

<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Your paid search campaigns didn’t suddenly get worse. The system around them changed.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">CPCs are up. CTRs are down.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">And most teams are responding the same way:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Optimize more. Test more. push harder.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But the issue isn’t effort. It’s that users aren’t behaving the same way anymore.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">They’re not searching. They’re asking.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">AI is answering questions before people ever click.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">Now, here’s the important part: Paid search still works.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">In fact, for newer brands without strong organic visibility, it’s often the fastest way to capture demand.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">But it’s no longer the first touchpoint.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">In my next webinar I will break down what’s happening and how to adapt.</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">​<a href="https://e22d5796.click.convertkit-mail4.com/qdu3qxr927t7h4p6xvgflh8gk2pvku4hplm9/vqh3hrho0wrlnpbg/aHR0cHM6Ly9hZHZhbmNlZC5ucGRpZ2l0YWwuY29tL3BhaWQtc2VhcmNoLWlzbnQtd2hhdC1pdC11c2VkLXRvLWJlLWxpdmUtd2ViaW5hci8_" target="_blank" class="ck-link" rel="noopener noreferrer" url-id="1846231088"><strong>Paid Search Isn’t What It Used to Be: The LLM Shift Explained</strong></a>​</p>

<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">You’ll learn:</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Why paid search feels less predictable (even when it’s working)</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ How AI is intercepting users earlier in the journey</p>
<p class="" style="margin-bottom:1em">✔ Where paid search still delivers the most value</p>

Morgan Stanley is one of the largest financial institutions in the world and happens to be one of the longest standing investment banks on Wall Street. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">It may appear Morgan Stanley is late to the game, but the organization is coming in hot and heavy. That type of pricing pressure should force the hand of other players in the market, which could lead to more inflows over time. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">I find it interesting that we are still getting &#8220;barbell news&#8221; in the bitcoin industry. The traditional financial firms want bitcoin to be a grown up asset they can package and sell to their clients, while the most violent criminals and terrorists in the world are flocking to the asset as a last resort to solve their unique problems.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">It may be uncomfortable for people to recognize but this is what true product-market fit looks like. Bitcoin is attractive to different people for different reasons. If you need to store economic value for a period of time, bitcoin is a great option. If you need to prevent others from taking that economic value, bitcoin may in the only option.</p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">It is exciting to see how far we have come in the last 15 years or so.
